$comment: The CLOSED set of installable modules this repository may publish, and the
facts each release is checked against. A package absent from this file
cannot be built or published by `release-module.yml` — the workflow resolves
its target here and fails closed, so adding a publishable module is a
reviewed diff rather than a dispatch-time string.
`dotmac-kernel` and `dotmac-ui` are deliberately NOT here: they have their
own workflows with their own inspection rules (a kernel wheel must ship
compiled CSS; a module must not). One workflow pretending to cover both
would have to weaken whichever check the other cannot satisfy.
kernel_floor is the EARLIEST kernel that can actually load and register
the module — the highest of everything the module needs, not one fixed
rule. Two things set it:
1. the release that allocated its schema in MIGRATION_OWNER_LEDGER; an
earlier kernel raises UnallocatedNamespaceError and the module cannot
register at all;
2. the release that added any kernel CAPABILITY the manifest consumes —
e.g. ADR-0023's `platform_tables`, added in a49; an earlier kernel
raises TypeError at import, before the allocation check is reached.
For most modules (1) is the answer and (2) does not apply. Where both
apply the higher wins, and tests/architecture/test_kernel_version_sync.py
keeps the two cases in separate, reasoned maps so neither is silent.
Either way registry verification can only pass once that kernel is
published.
Listed for the ERP-first ticket adoption programme (ADR-0017's
2026-08-13 ticketing amendment). Until this entry existed the module
was unpublishable, so no product could pin it and the dossier's
`first_cutover` was unreachable by construction.
kernel_floor is a49, NOT the a39 that allocated mod_tkt. This module is
dual-plane (ADR-0023) and its manifest passes `platform_tables`, which
a49 added — an earlier kernel raises TypeError at import, before the
allocation check runs. It is the one module whose floor is set by a
kernel capability rather than by its own namespace row.
`alembic` is in allowed_requires and is NOT a packaging slip:
`dotmac_ticketing.linking`'s per-plane link helpers emit DDL into a
CONSUMING product's migration, so Alembic is imported at runtime by
them rather than used as a dev tool. The other modules ship no such
helper and correctly forbid it.
mod_files is allocated in kernel a54, and that allocation is ALSO the
floor: ADR-0023's dual-plane platform_tables landed earlier, in a53, so
the module's own namespace row is the higher of the two requirements.
This is the ordinary case; dotmac-ticketing is the exception.
The bulk-import run ledger (ADR-0025). kernel_floor is a50, the
release that allocated mod_imports; no kernel capability raises it
above its own allocation, so this is an ordinary case rather than a
ticketing/files-style exception.
No alembic in allowed_requires: this module ships its own im lineage
but emits no DDL into a CONSUMING product's migration, so Alembic is a
packaging input rather than a runtime import.
